newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - March 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post front - March 12.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on March 12:

WASHINGTON - Senate Republicans reversed course and agreed to broaden a probe of illegal campaign fund-raising practices to cover legal but "improper" practices, including unregistered soft money contributions to political parties.

WASHINGTON - The White House and Justice Department tried to defuse their dispute over whether President Clinton was adequately warned about alleged Chinese attempts to influence last year's U.S. congressional elections, dismissing the episode as a misunderstanding among busy mid-level aides.

WASHINGTON - President Clinton unveiled a $300 million economic stimulus proposal for the District that would offer federal grants and tax incentives to businesses that invest in neglected neighborhoods.

WASHINGTON - D.C.'s neediest -- from the elderly to recovering addicts -- brace for budget blows as officials prepare to implement $19.3 million in health and other human services cuts mandated by the control board.
WASHINGTON - The FBI assigned 50 agents to the Prince George's County Police Department for a two-month blitz against murderers, drug dealers and armed robbers.
BRUSSELS - Defense analysts in Europe and the United States say the Clinton administration's estimated costs for NATO expansion may be too optimistic.

WASHINGTON - The Environmental Protection Agency illegally tried to force 12 northeastern states and the District of Colombia to adopt emission standards on new cars sold there, a federal appeals panel ruled.
WASHINGTON - Small, silent strokes may cause much of the memory loss and dementia that afflicts people with Alzheimer's disease.
